newsitem.title: UK: Britain's FTSE set to crack 4,000 in coming week.
newsitem.headline: Britain's FTSE set to crack 4,000 in coming week.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 share index, which surged to record highs on Friday after weaker-than- expected U.S. economic reports, could be poised to crack the 4,000-point barrier next week, analysts said on Friday.

The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of Britain's 100 largest companies set a new all-time high of 3,970.5 points in afternoon dealings, up 37.9 points on the day and bringing its gain for the week to 77.5 points.
The U.S. data, which sent U.S. bonds soaring, reinvigorated the London market which set repeated records this week as the Dow rose and leading companies posted favourable results.
With Wall Street near record highs and funds flush with cash, strategists said the market was on a firm footing despite continued low trading volumes.

"The 4,000-point level should not present much of a barrier...we've cracked 3,950 points and we are looking at the potential to see acceleration past 4,000," said David Sneddon, global trading technical analyst at Credit Suisse.

Sneddon said the break beyond 4,000 could open the way for a move as high as 4,120 points, but others cautioned the market could run out of steam, even if some funds, fearful of missing out on the sudden upturn, began to pump cash into the market.

"We should see 4,000 points next week but levels significantly above that could be hard to maintain," said Richard Jeffrey, strategist at Charterhouse Tilney. "We are approaching fully-valued levels."

Analysts said the U.S. data, showing a lower-than-expected 0.1 percent rise in consumer prices in August, would reinforce hopes the U.S. Fed would either delay or restrict a widely- expected 25 basis-point rate hike. Philip Isherwood, UK strategist at Kleinwort Benson, said U.S. monetary policy was little obstacle to further gains on the FTSE, especially if the Fed packaged a rate rise as pre-emptive. "UK corporate results have been OK on the whole, sterling is behaving and if people really believe that a 25 basis point rate rise has been discounted, then there is nothing really next week which could upset the market," Isherwood said.
He cautioned, however, that the lacklustre performance of UK gilts, hit by worries Chancellor Kenneth Clarke might indulge in a pre-election rate cut, could put a brake on the market.

With U.S. rate worries dwindling, analysts said investors would continue to focus on company results, after upbeat half-year reports from Kingfisher, BTR, British Aerospace, Legal and General and Williams Holdings.
"The tone of company statements, particularly from the manufacturing sector, has been good and that's what we'll be listening for next week," Jeffrey said.
Next week the flow of UK corporate results is set to slow slightly but the list of companies reporting includes Tesco , P&O, Next and British Biotech.

Players will also keep a weather eye on Wednesday's UK retail sales and Tuesday's UK public sector borrowing requirement data, although analysts said those figures, and Thursday's money supply news, should prove uncontroversial.
A statement on monthly trends for September from the Confederation of British Industry on Friday could, however, prove more decisive.
U.S. figures next week include U.S. business inventories on Monday, industry output for August on Tuesday and housing starts on Thursday.
